source_refs.title: Connect a Bluetooth device with your Mac - Apple Support
source_refs.section: Connect a Bluetooth device with your Mac
source_refs.applicability: Mac; steps for devices other than Apple wireless keyboards, mice, and trackpads
source_refs.verified_excerpt: Make sure the device is turned on and discoverable
source_refs.model_visible_text: On Mac: Make sure the device is turned on and discoverable. The device's documentation explains how. Choose Apple menu, then System Settings. Click Bluetooth in the sidebar. You may need to scroll down. Move the pointer over the device in the list and click Connect. If prompted, click Accept, or enter the number sequence shown and press Enter. You can also connect a Bluetooth device to your Mac by clicking in Control Center and selecting the device.

source_refs.title: Pair a Bluetooth device in Windows | Microsoft Support
source_refs.section: Pair a Bluetooth device in Windows
source_refs.applicability: Windows 11; the Windows device needs Bluetooth, built in or from a USB adapter
source_refs.verified_excerpt: Follow additional instructions if they appear, then select Done.
source_refs.model_visible_text: On Windows 11: Turn on the device and make it discoverable. The method depends on the device, so check its documentation or the manufacturer's website. On the taskbar, click the Network, Sound, or Battery icon next to the time and date. Select the Manage Bluetooth devices chevron on the Bluetooth quick setting, then select the device under New devices. If New devices doesn't appear, scroll through Your devices. Follow additional instructions if they appear, then select Done.

source_refs.title: Pair a Bluetooth device in Windows | Microsoft Support
source_refs.section: Bluetooth must be turned on; device not in list; after pairing
source_refs.verified_excerpt: the Bluetooth devices discovery setting might need to be set to
source_refs.model_visible_text: On Windows 11: Bluetooth must be turned on. Use the Bluetooth quick setting, or go to Settings, then Bluetooth & devices. If the Bluetooth device isn't displayed in the list, the Bluetooth devices discovery setting might need to be set to Advanced. To learn how, see Fix Bluetooth problems in Windows. When Bluetooth is turned on, the Bluetooth device and the Windows device automatically connect anytime the two devices are in range of each other.

source_refs.title: Find & set up Bluetooth devices near your Android device - Android Help
source_refs.section: Pairing a Bluetooth accessory through Settings
source_refs.applicability: Android; some steps work only on Android 15 and up; some steps need supporting hardware
source_refs.model_visible_text: On Android: From the top of the screen, swipe down. Touch and hold Bluetooth. Tap Pair new device. If there's no Pair new device, check under Available devices, or tap More, then Refresh. Tap the name of the Bluetooth device. Follow the on-screen instructions. If you see a notification to pair, automatically connect your Bluetooth devices with Fast Pair. Some of these steps work only on Android 15 and up.
